purpose: Search for current university-authoritative Study.com receiving awards, university endorsement of a specific provider equivalency guide, or an explicit policy awarding the original recommended quantity and level as elective/category credit.

method.access: Public web search/open/click through the connected search service, plus read-only inspection of existing local source captures and conditional options.
method.newCaptureFormat: Structured review of native rendered public-web extracts; not a raw origin response or a full article capture.

outcome.summary: No additional authoritative Study.com receiving award was established by the public sources reviewed. Keep existing Study.com receiving candidates conditional. This is an evidence limit, not a claim that TESU rejects Study.com or that no private agreement exists.

sources.publisher: Thomas Edison State University current Undergraduate Catalog
sources.quote: The elective category may be satisfied by almost any college credits. Academic policies should be reviewed for limitation of credits.
sources.finding: The page permits broad elective choice and says featured GE courses are examples with other university-approved alternatives. It retains the academic-policy restrictions and links to the GE course-category lists.
sources.limit: This describes degree placement for accepted credit. It does not independently award unreviewed Study.com credit, guarantee its source quantity/level, or turn a discipline label into a TESU GE category decision.

sources.quote: For Study.com, we will not accept the credit from the ACE transcript, only the Study.com transcript is acceptable for credit review.

sources.limit: The agreement concerns the official transcript channel. It does not publish a course-equivalency matrix.

searchCoverage: University-domain searches for Study.com plus equivalency, equivalencies, course guide, transfer guide, articulation, BSBA, Working Scholars, studycom and PDF variants.
ACE searches for TESU plus Study.com or SDCM identifiers, the current institution inventory, and current selected upper-division Study exhibits.
Current university approved-provider and provider-evaluation pages, transfer-pathway index, ACE/NCCRS acceptance policy, transfer-credit policy and business-degree elective policy.
Provider-specific school guide and support article inspected as secondary evidence, not substituted for the receiving institution.
requiredEvidenceToClose: A current TESU-published or TESU-submitted course award or an authenticated public articulation appendix naming the Study.com source identity/version, receiving course or explicitly typed elective/category, receiving quantity/level and applicable catalog/period.

Alternatively, a university policy expressly awarding qualifying original ACE/NCCRS quantities and levels to a defined elective/category under named conditions. The general policies reviewed here do not make that guarantee.

Retain original course quantity/units, receiving quantity/level, provider approval, recommendation dates, placement, noncollegiate caps, residency and duplicate-learning rules as separate evidence dimensions.
studentImpact: Existing fully supported Sophia receiving awards can continue to drive the current business expansion. DegreeSteps owns the remaining Study.com equivalency research. Personal transcript evaluation remains a distinct student step; this review creates no blanket per-course written-approval homework.
